title: Kimsuky Malware Targets South Korean Reserve Forces With Fake Training Notifications
content_md:
This article discusses malware attributed to North Korean APT group Kimsuky (APT43) that is believed to target South Korean reserve forces. The malware disguises itself as a "Local Reserve Forces Training Participation Notice."

South Korean Reserve Forces (ROK Reserve Forces, ROK RF) are military reserve units within the Republic of Korea Armed Forces. Reserve members are individuals who have completed active duty and transitioned to reserve status, or those who have completed supplementary service. During wartime, reserves are activated to active duty.

The article examines Kimsuky's continued interest in South Korean reserve forces. The group is known for targeting South Korean military, government, and academic institutions with social engineering campaigns and malware. This campaign specifically uses fake reserve force training notifications as the lure vector, likely delivered via phishing emails or messaging to reserve members.

Article Link: [Kimsuky malware targeting reserve forces - training participation notice lure](https://malware.news/t/kimsuky/125000#post_1)
